correctness.rationale: For disk radial perturbation, the two chord endpoints at polar angles θ±α remain transverse since sinα>0; implicit differentiation of the line intersection gives D_α f=(f(θ+α)+f(θ-α))/sinα. Thus λ_m=2cos(mα)/sinα, and combined data have squared Fourier multiplier W_m=Σ_j4cos²(mα_j)/sin²α_j. The closure H of the integer orbit of a=(α_j/π) in T^k contains b=(1/2,...,1/2) iff every annihilating integer character h·a in Z has h·b in Z; so the infimum W_m>0 iff some integer relation has odd sum. Rational common zeros satisfy m=(q_j/2)(odd) for each even denominator; intersection exists iff all v_2(q_j) agree, and exact indices are odd multiples of lcm(q_j/2). For two offsets α and 2α with 0<α<π/4, substitute z=cos²(mα) to get W=1+csc²α+(2z-sin²α)^2/(sin²α cos²α), giving uniform lower bound and exact irrational sharpness by dense rotation; convexity in z makes upper coefficient attained at m=0. Check rational (π/6,π/4) table gives min4 and max24. Finite examples supplement analytic character theorem and the square identity.
